pricing.q: Do you offer a discount for booking multiple lessons at once?
pricing.a: Not as an upfront bundle discount — lessons are simply pay-as-you-go. But after your first lesson, if you're ready to commit to ongoing coaching, I offer a structured 8-week program for $480, which works out to a better value than booking single lessons indefinitely.

contact.q: How quickly will I hear back?
contact.a: Usually within a day — often much sooner.

contact.q: Do you offer a first-lesson discount?
contact.a: No special first-lesson discount, but there's no commitment required — book a single lesson and decide from there. If you want to go further after that, ask about the 8-week program.

contact.q: What should I bring to my first lesson?
contact.a: Water, comfortable athletic or court shoes, and sunscreen. If you already have a paddle, bring it — if not, just mention that when you reach out.

areas.q: Do you travel to me, or do I come to you?
areas.a: Lift Pickleball is based in Walnut Creek, and most lessons happen at a court that's convenient for both of us somewhere in the surrounding East Bay. Reach out with your city and we'll find a spot nearby.

areas.q: What if my city isn't listed?
areas.a: The cities above aren't exhaustive. If you're anywhere in the greater East Bay, get in touch and we'll figure out a court that works for both of us.

areas.q: Is there an extra fee for lessons outside Walnut Creek?

lessons.q: I'm not very athletic — is that a problem?
lessons.a: Not at all. Most students start exactly where you are, and lessons are built around your current fitness level, not some assumed baseline. We'll work at a pace that challenges you without wearing you out.

lessons.q: Do I need to commit to a bunch of lessons, or can I just try one?
lessons.a: Just book one. There's no package or commitment required to get started — see how it feels, then decide if you want to keep going. If you do want to commit further down the road, ask about the 8-week program.
Lessons are played outdoors, so we'll reschedule together if the weather doesn't cooperate — just keep an eye out for a text or email from me if conditions look iffy.

lessons.q: What if I have a bad knee, shoulder, or other physical limitation?
lessons.a: Let me know ahead of time and we'll adjust the pace, drills, and movement accordingly. I'm not a medical professional, so if you have a specific injury concern, it's worth checking with your doctor first — but plenty of students manage around physical limitations just fine.

lessons.q: Do you coach kids or teens?
lessons.a: Lift Pickleball's focus is adult students, but I'm open to coaching teens on a case-by-case basis — reach out and tell me a bit about the student and we'll figure out if it's a good fit.

lessons.q: How is a private lesson different from a free clinic or just playing open play?
lessons.a: Open play and free clinics are great for reps, but nobody's watching your specific game. A lesson means personalized feedback on exactly what's holding your game back, with a coach who adjusts in real time instead of generic group instruction.
